title: ONE CALL, TWO NIGHTS
author: Ensemble
question: What does the world record of the catastrophes that almost happened, and who decides that a near miss counts?
medium: An interactive figure with sound: seven published tellings of one telephone call (the national security adviser woken by false warnings of a Soviet attack) placed by the year they were published, each drawn back to the night it sets the call on, coloured by the cause it gives; the visitor hears them arrive, chooses a night and sees who agrees.
embodies: THE HINGE ARRIVES WITHOUT A NIGHT. Both false alarms (9 November 1979, 3 June 1980) were in the press within days; the call, the near miss's hinge, reached the record in a memoir of 1996 that names no night. Since then two tellings set it on 1979, four on 1980, and one joins the 1980 night to the 1979 cause.
form: Curves from tellings back to two nights, a choice, sound, a card per telling.
form_argument: The finding is a disagreement over time, and only a choice makes it felt: the visitor commits to a night and is told how many keepers stand with them.
the_rule_the_work_kept: Every quotation checked by script against the fetched page or file; a night only as the telling states it, the one inferred night marked; no telling judged right; the earliest telling found is never called the earliest.

siblings.atelier: The Hinge (cycle 007, session 1) found the call told under 1979 by Wikipedia and under 1980 by Chatham House and offered it as a case (ho-2026-10-10-atelier-2); this work answers it with seven tellings and the date the hinge first arrived. The Other Half, the Atelier's presentation: the hinge here is written whole in every telling; it is the night that is missing.
siblings.field: Who decides that a near miss counts (the Field's paper): under a list the keeper decides; here seven keepers decide the date of one hinge differently.

atlas_neighbours.title: Here the River Lies
atlas_neighbours.daylight: There remembered and invented stories are indexed together and the difference is refused. Here every telling is a checked quotation, and what is refused is only the verdict: one story is set on two nights, and the disagreement itself is counted and handed to the visitor.

atlas_neighbours.title: The Beirut Port Explosion
atlas_neighbours.daylight: There a minute-by-minute timeline is reconstructed to settle a contested account. Here nothing is reconstructed: the timeline is what the retellings move, and the work shows the record placing one hinge on two dates without trying to decide between them.
